rows.description: A school-age child presses the tongue against a cheek while concentrating or hiding a joke, and older people use it to show something is tongue-in-cheek. The meaning depends on shared context.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Blank face at bullying or shame [Regulating]
rows.description: A child keeps a blank, rigid face when teased to avoid giving a reaction, which can hide real hurt. Adults check in privately and let the child know they can ask for help.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A school-age child delivers a joke with a deadpan face, making it funnier for those who know the style but confusing others. A small signal like a twinkle helps show it is a joke.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Bowing the head and namaste in India [Mismatch]
rows.description: A child learns to bow the head slightly with namaste to greet elders as respect, which differs from head-bowing in shame. Context and culture decide whether it signals reverence or submission.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A school-age child sees a teacher tilt the head and reads curiosity or sympathy, though it can also be doubt. Body and tone add to the meaning.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: curiosity, doubt, empathy

rows.description: A child drops the shoulders after a loss or disappointing marks, showing sadness or defeat. A warm word helps more than telling the child to cheer up.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A school-age child sees a friend lift one shoulder and reads uncertainty, shyness or a half-hearted maybe. It is a weak signal, so asking clarifies.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child holds hands behind the back, in school parade or when hiding something, and it may signal respect, nervousness or concealment. It is not proof of guilt.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: admiration, anxiety, guilt

rows.description: A school-age child sees a teacher with hands on hips and reads authority or impatience, but it may also be resting. Tone and words add meaning.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child snaps the fingers in rhythm or to call attention, and rubs the hands from cold or eager anticipation. Meaning depends on context, and snapping at people can seem rude.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
